sourceEvidence.label: Camisaria Mendes licensing and contractual suspension evidence

assessment.summary: Replace a hidden shutdown path with a disclosed entitlement state machine, signed leases, grace periods, and non-destructive restriction.

nonNegotiables: No hidden URL, master credential, remote shell, or destructive action.
No deletion or mutation of customer business history during suspension.
Administrative login, backup, export, and offboarding remain possible.
Contractual notice and cure periods are authoritative over technical defaults.
assumptions: The customer controls the production host.
Source-code delivery and root access have not yet been confirmed.
Legal validity depends on the final contract and must be reviewed by counsel.
Latency, uptime, and grace-period budgets have not been supplied.

opportunities.title: Introduce explicit contractual entitlement enforcement
opportunities.summary: Represent payment status as a signed, auditable, reversible product entitlement instead of a hidden backdoor.
opportunities.diagnosis: The customer-controlled deployment has no licensing boundary; any purely local shutdown mechanism is both privileged and removable by the host owner.

evidence.claim: The Node router owns all business operations but has no entitlement gate.
The application code and configuration run on the deployment host.
An administrator with control of the host can patch or replace a local license check.

desiredInvariants: Only vendor-signed entitlement states can enable paid functionality.
Vendor-service unavailability never causes immediate suspension.
Suspension blocks new business operations but preserves history, admin access, backups, exports, and offboarding.
Every billing transition, notice, lease, restriction, and reactivation is auditable.
The installation sends no customer personal data that is unnecessary for licensing.
The product accurately documents when client root access can bypass enforcement.

options.title: Contract-only enforcement
options.summary: Rely on notices and contractual remedies without a remote technical shutdown.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The customer continues to control the entire installation.

tradeoffs.assessment: No privileged remote channel is introduced, but there is no technical enforcement.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review access boundaries and confirm no vendor credential remains in the installation.
No additional measurement beyond the existing baseline is required.

tradeoffs.assessment: No vendor licensing outage can affect the client system.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm the installation operates without vendor connectivity.

tradeoffs.assessment: Billing collection remains a contractual/manual process.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise notice, cure, and termination procedures with counsel and operations.
Align invoice, contract, and offboarding documentation.

residualRisks: The customer can continue using the installation while in default.

workPackages: Define notices, cure, termination, and collection workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: No undisclosed vendor access remains in the product.

options.title: Signed license leases with graceful restriction
options.summary: A vendor service issues short-lived signed entitlements; the client installation enforces a documented state machine.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A server-side gate can consistently restrict business writes.
Signed leases resist simple configuration edits but remain patchable by a host owner with source access.

tradeoffs.assessment: The private signing key stays with the vendor; customer-hosted code contains only a public key. Root/source access can still remove the check.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test forged, replayed, expired, downgraded, and revoked leases plus deliberate local tampering.

tradeoffs.assessment: Background refresh adds infrequent network work; request paths read a bounded local state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure refresh latency and API p95 with cached entitlement checks.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only a small signed lease and state cache are retained.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare process RSS under the smoke workload.

tradeoffs.assessment: The license service is a new dependency, bounded by cached leases and a contractual grace period.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Simulate service loss, DNS failure, clock skew, restart, and grace expiry.

tradeoffs.assessment: Billing integration, signing-key protection, tenant audit, notifications, and reactivation become vendor responsibilities.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run activation, overdue, suspension, reactivation, key rotation, and disaster-recovery drills.

tradeoffs.assessment: Backend routing, admin UI, deployment configuration, contract, and billing workflow all change.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Roll out in observe-only mode before enabling restriction for any customer.

residualRisks: A customer with root and source can patch out the enforcement.
Compromise of the vendor signing/control plane can affect multiple customers.

workPackages: Build signed lease issuer and verifier.
Add notice, audit, grace, and reactivation flows.
acceptanceCriteria: Vendor outage does not immediately restrict service.
Forged or stale leases do not enable paid operations.
migrationNotes: Start with observe-only telemetry and active leases.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Issue long-lived active leases and disable restriction while retaining audit records.

options.title: Vendor-hosted essential service
options.summary: Keep an indispensable business capability under vendor control while the rest runs on the client host.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The client cannot fully restore the contracted capability by only patching the local host, though it could reimplement the remote service.

tradeoffs.assessment: Enforcement authority is outside the client host, but vendor APIs and tenant isolation become high-value targets.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model tenant isolation, authorization, abuse, outage containment, and API replay.

tradeoffs.assessment: Critical operations gain a network hop and serialization.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark the selected operation from the client region with explicit p95/p99 targets.

tradeoffs.assessment: Client memory may stay similar; the vendor service adds independent capacity needs.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Capacity-test the vendor service and compare client RSS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Product availability now depends on vendor uptime and network connectivity.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Define SLOs and test timeouts, retries, partial degradation, and regional outage.

tradeoffs.assessment: The vendor operates production infrastructure, on-call, billing, security, backup, and incident response.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete an operational readiness review before contracting the dependency.

tradeoffs.assessment: A business capability must be extracted behind a versioned remote API.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Dual-run the local and remote paths before cutover and maintain a rollback protocol.

residualRisks: Vendor outage affects every licensed customer.
The architecture is no longer fully self-hosted.
A determined client can reimplement the missing service.

acceptanceCriteria: Local patching alone cannot restore the contracted capability.
Vendor outage behavior matches the SLA.
No customer business data beyond the agreed scope leaves the client host.
migrationNotes: Requires explicit SaaS disclosure and data-flow review.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Re-enable the local capability during the agreed rollback window.

opportunities.recommendation: The user selected the minimal offline variant of signed enforcement: short-lived one-time suspend/activate commands verified locally with an Ed25519 public key.

openQuestions: Will the customer receive repository/source access in addition to root access?
Is the transaction a perpetual sale/assignment or a recurring software license?
Which operations remain available during restriction?
What notice, cure, reactivation, export, and offboarding obligations will the contract establish?
